title: Micropatterning on silicon elastomer \(PDMS) with deep UVs
protocol: Wash the PDMS in Ethanol 70% for 15 minutes.
Dry the PDMS under air flow.
Illuminate the PDMS with a deep UV lamp for 5 minutes, maintaining a distance of about 5 cm from the lamp.
Weigh EDC and NHS powders: use 11.5 mg NHS and 19.2 mg EDC per 1 mL solution.
Dissolve the weighed powder in a 0.05 M MES + 0.5 M NaCl buffer at pH 6.0.
Cover the PDMS substrate with the EDC/NHS solution.
Incubate the PDMS substrate covered with EDC/NHS solution for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Rinse the surface with PBS followed by H2O.
Cover the surface with a 0.5 mg/mL PLL-g-PEG solution in Hepes buffer (pH 8.5).
Incubate the PDMS substrate covered with PLL-g-PEG for 3 hours or overnight at room temperature in a humid chamber to avoid evaporation.
Wash the surface with H2O after incubation.
Store passivated surfaces in water at +4°C for several days.
Wear nitrile gloves.
Wash the mask with 70% Ethanol using a soft tissue, repeat washing steps if necessary.
Place the quartz mask with its metal side facing the UV lamp.
Illuminate the surface of the quartz mask for 5 minutes to clean and make it hydrophilic.
Add the passivated PDMS substrate onto the mask on the metal side, avoiding bubbles.
Put the quartz mask with its quartz side facing the lamp (PDMS on bottom).
Illuminate both sides for 5-10 minutes.
Carefully and very slowly peel off the PDMS from the mask.
Add water to facilitate peeling off the PDMS.
Incubate the illuminated surface for 1 hour at room temperature with 25 μg/mL of fibronectin in 100 mM NaHCO3 (pH 8.5).
Collect cells using EDTA at a concentration of 0.02% in PBS.
Rinse the EDTA solution with pre-warmed and pH-equilibrated culture medium.
Resuspend the collected cells using a 1 mL micropipette to separate them well.
Add between 100,000 to 200,000 cells for a 25 mm coverslip or a 6-well plate well in a small volume of approximately 500 μL.
Wash unattached cells 20-30 min after plating with equilibrated hot medium.
Add medium from one side to create a gentle flow over the cells.
Aspirate medium from the other side simultaneously.
Spread cells on patterns 1 hour after plating.
Attach patterned silicone membrane to the device.
Cut a square piece of PDMS and empty the center to obtain a four-walled chamber.
Use silicone grease to bind the chamber on top of the patterned silicone membrane.
Plate the cells as described above.
Close the chamber with a coverslip to avoid evaporation.
